title: Application Bootstrap
description: The tour starts where the browser does: main.tsx applies the persisted color theme before first paint, resolves which game-server dataset (Homecoming, Rebirth, or Thunderspy) is active, installs a chunk-error auto-reload, and mounts the App component inside an error fallback. App.tsx itself is deliberately tiny — it just hands control to the TanStack Router. This split keeps side-effectful startup work (theme, dataset, error handling) out of the React tree.
languageLesson: Vite + React apps bootstrap through createRoot in a plain .tsx entry module. Work done here runs exactly once, before React renders — the right place for theme application and global error hooks that must not flash or re-run.

title: Routing and Layout Shell
description: router.tsx defines the TanStack Router route tree: a root wrapped in MainLayout, planner and shared-build routes, and a settings subtree. MainLayout is the structural skeleton every page lives inside — header, stats dashboard, info panels, banners, modals, the enhancement picker, and mobile navigation, plus global hotkeys. Understanding this file tells you where almost every visible UI element is mounted.
languageLesson: TanStack Router builds routes as typed objects rather than JSX, giving compile-time-checked paths and search params — a contrast to React Router's component-based route declarations.

title: The Domain Vocabulary: Types Layer
description: With 121 files importing it, types/index.ts is the single most depended-upon module in the codebase — the shared vocabulary everything else speaks. build.ts defines the Build model (powerset selections, slotting, attack chains, versioned export formats), while power.ts is the largest type module, describing Power, Powerset, and every effect shape the game data can express (damage, mez, DoT, defense/resistance by-type, summons, movement). Learn these types first and every other layer becomes readable.
languageLesson: TypeScript discriminated unions shine for game effects: each effect shape carries a discriminant field, and type-guard helpers let calculation code narrow to the exact shape safely instead of duck-typing.

title: Build State: The Zustand Stores
description: buildStore.ts is the beating heart of user state: archetype and powerset selection, power picks, enhancement slotting, incarnates, and per-server persisted builds, with dataset sync, undo checkpoints, and import/export wiring. Its sibling uiStore.ts (2,100+ lines) owns everything ephemeral — modals, theme, planner layout, tooltips, toasts, exemplar settings. The stores/index.ts barrel is imported by 72 files, making these stores the second-most-connected hub after the types layer.
languageLesson: Zustand stores are plain hooks with selector functions: components subscribe to a narrow slice (useStore(s => s.powers)) and only re-render when that slice changes — critical for a planner where one store backs 150+ component instances.

title: Game Data Layer: Three Servers, One API
description: This is the project's signature architectural trick. dataset.ts defines the Dataset contract and a single active-dataset indirection (loadDataset/getActiveDataset) so Homecoming, Rebirth, and Thunderspy data swap transparently at runtime. Facades like powersets.ts, archetypes.ts, and at-tables.ts route every lookup through whichever dataset is active — at-tables.ts even uses JavaScript Proxies so pre-existing indexed reads keep working unchanged. The data/index.ts barrel (fan-in 80) is the door the rest of the app walks through.
languageLesson: A Proxy can turn a module-level constant into a live indirection: AT_TABLES looks like a plain object, but every property read is routed to the currently active dataset at call time — a migration technique that preserves old import paths while changing what backs them.

title: How Game Data Is Modeled
description: The data layer's README explains the layering discipline: generated/ output from the binary game-data pipeline is authoritative, overrides are the exception, and it documents the composed-file shapes. atomic-effect.ts is the conceptual core beneath it — a closed AtomicEffect schema with compact wire encoding, identity/structural keys for differential comparison, and the attrib-to-(effectType, subType) bridge that turns exported game power templates into flat lists of atomic effects. This mirrors how the game itself models a power: not named fields, but a flat array of atoms.

title: The Calculation Engine
description: character-totals.ts is the heavyweight of the codebase — highest fan-out at 34 imports — aggregating set bonuses, active power effects, procs, accolades, incarnates, and buff-pet auras into final character stats with per-stat breakdowns. damage.ts handles power damage from AT scale tables, DoT tick expectations (including geometric cancel-on-miss math), and Arcana cast time. The calculations/index.ts barrel exposes roughly 140 symbols, making this the app's computational public API. Everything the Stats Dashboard shows flows out of here.

title: Enhancement and Set-Bonus Math
description: Building on the engine from Step 7, enhancement-values.ts implements the game's enhancement rules: IO value schedules by level, Enhancement Diversification (ED) diminishing-returns curves, exemplar scaling, and per-power bonus aggregation including Alpha incarnate combination. io-sets.ts is the facade that turns raw dataset set data into typed IOSet objects, and set-bonuses.ts aggregates bonuses across the whole build with Rule-of-5 cap tracking — the rule that only five copies of the same bonus count.

title: Proc Mechanics
description: Procs — enhancements with a chance to fire an effect — get their own subsystem. proc-data.ts is the central proc database and math library: every IO-set proc entry, the full PPM (procs-per-minute) chance formula, area-factor geometry, and stacking resolution. power-proc-damage.ts computes the flat per-cast damage of slotted damage procs, deliberately shared by both the damage display and the Attack Chain builder's DPS so the two can never diverge — a good example of the project's single-source-of-truth discipline.

title: The Reactive Bridge: Calculation Hooks
description: Between the pure calculation engine and the UI sits the hooks layer. useCalculatedStats.ts exposes the unified character-totals calculation to React: stat conversion, per-stat breakdowns, Rule-of-5 tracking, and over-cap reasons — all backed by a module-level single-entry cache so that 150+ component instances share one calculation run instead of each recomputing it. The hooks/index.ts barrel (fan-in 20) is how components consume this layer.
languageLesson: A module-level cache keyed on a dependency tuple sits outside React entirely: every hook instance checks the same cache entry, so a state change triggers one expensive recomputation, not one per subscribed component. This pattern fixed a real ~1s UI stall in this codebase.

title: The Planner UI
description: Now the pieces assemble on screen. PlannerPage.tsx composes the power sections, docked/popped-out info panel, and set-bonus popup into a user-customizable multi-column grid with drag-to-reorder and column resizing. PowerRow.tsx is the workhorse row for each taken power (slots, toggle state, perma-ring, set bonuses); EnhancementPicker.tsx is the slotting UI with IO sets, procs, and set-bonus previews; InfoPanel.tsx is the largest display component, rendering full power detail; and StatsDashboard.tsx is the central read-out of the entire calculation pipeline from Steps 7-10.

title: Import, Export, and Build Sharing
description: Finally, builds leave and enter the app. ExportImportModal.tsx handles every path: shareable build-hash links, Mids Reborn .mbd/.mxd imports, in-game export parsing, and forum/popmenu/print exports. The mids-import module parses the competing planner's file format so players can migrate. On the cloud side, supabase.ts creates the singleton client and sharedBuilds.ts implements the shared-builds repository — publishing, search, favorites, view counts, and anonymous owner tokens — which BuildsPage.tsx surfaces as a searchable community build browser.
